newsitem.title: USA: Former Orange Cty budget director gets probation.
newsitem.headline: Former Orange Cty budget director gets probation.

text.p: A judge on Monday sentenced former Orange County, Calif., budget director Ronald Rubino to probation in a deal that averts his retrial on felony charges stemming from the county's bankruptcy crisis.
Rubino, 44, pleaded no contest to a single charge he falsified a county public record in violation of state law.
Superior Court Judge J. Stephen Czuleger sentenced Rubino to 100 hours of community service and two years of unsupervised probation.

As part of the deal, the Orange County District Attorney agreed to drop two existing felony counts against Rubino. The counts that were dropped carried a maximum penalty of nine years in state prison.

Rubino was indicted by a county grand jury in December 1995 on two felony charges accusing him of helping former county Treasurer Robert Citron divert funds from other government agencies for the county's benefit.
His trial, the first criminal trial to arise from the county bankruptcy, began in August but ended in a mistrial Sept. 13. A new trial had been set to begin next week.

Attorneys involved in the case said Rubino would be able to petition the court at the end of the first year of his probation to withdraw his no contest plea and enter a plea of innocent. The charge would then be dismissed.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
Citron, who pleaded guilty in April 1995 to six felony charges stemming from the bankruptcy, is awaiting sentencing. Other former and current county officials have yet to be tried.
